I know some people will say that all time great cannot be overrated but I disagree. Players can be amazing and still be overrated by the media and / or fans. Also in this convo we are only taking into account the top 25-30 guys all time, not just every other superstar.

Eh he's a weird one. I think he's a bit overrated in the underrated conversation. He seems to fall in the 15-25 range which seems right. He could score and rebound with the best of them, but he was a selfish player on offense, turned the ball over lots, couldn't pass to save his life, and despite some defensive weaknesses he has pretty well known as a poor defender. He has the resume of a top 10 player but he just isn't that guy.

He just wasn't that guy? You don't get 3 MVPs by accident, you also don't average 26 and 18 in the Finals vs 2 players everyone unanimously puts in the top 5 of NBA history without being "that guy". You don't beat the Lakers after Magic's historic rookie championship season in the first round averaging 31 and 18 then proceed to go to the Finals as the sixth man without being "that guy"

You're taking that "not that guy" statement way too literal and ignoring everything else that was said. He's one of the 20 best basketball players of all time. Which I said in my original post. Greg Ostertag. I know he's untouchable on this sub so bring on the downvotes, but he really wasn't that great.

hot take: every great that I didn't get to see live in their prime. I can't fully use the greatness of Bird, bill russell, kareem etc. with confidence - not because I think they're perfect, but because I only got to see their highlight tapes & legendary games. I often feel that Kobe's fame exceeds what he achieved and how good he was, not to say he wasn't an all time great, but a lot of fans have him top 5. I think it would be difficult to argue him as a top 10.
There's some of that, but I would argue a big part of the difference between perception and impact is fans over-rating shooting guards in general.

Scoring and athleticism, yeah. Hitting tough shots or the explosive breaks to the basket are really memorable. The tough ones are still only worth 2 though. The guys getting easy points in the paint aren't as celebrated but make a bigger difference winning games.
It's entertainment, at the end of the day. The more entertaining players will always get the subjective nod.

Eh. But Kobe was a 12x All Defensive player 15x All NBA so, there's more to his legacy than scoring. I was never a fan of his (Phoenix Sun supporter) but I'd look at anyone skeptically, who actually watched his games, that said that they'd have a hard time putting him in the top 10.
He hovers around there for me (the ten spot). He was very very good. I think people just value him as if he was on that MJ Bron level.

Casual fans aren't the same. There's a clear separation between he and Jordan. He and Lebron, that's where you'll get lots of debate. Even from active and former players. I don't like to compare era for this reason. Different rules. Different game.
And Kobe didn't deserve a single all-defensive team post 2003. His coach said that. He coasted on reputation. im from Boston, Smart did not deserve his dpoy either.

Kobe is a lot of people's goat because of his mentality more than anything. The people like someone that wants to compete night in and night out. Kobe never robbed anyone who paid for a ticket to see him play.

It's definitely Kobe. However, I don't think it's all that difficult to put him in the top 10. He's on the same tier as Duncan and Shaq imo, but not on the tier of Lebron/Jordan where so many people put them.

Came her for this. Kobe is definitely not anywhere close to being top 5 player. You can make a case for him being in the top 10 all time. But I've always rated him behind Duncan and Shaq (although not far behind). People are nostalgic about kobe, even before his death.

Same tier as Shaq? Sure. Duncan? Nope. Duncan is the most underrated all-time great. Honestly, if he spoke about intangibles like killer mentality and had an aggressive Big Ticket-like persona, without changing any of his accolades we would all be calling him top 5 all time.
Duncan was in a small market with an introverted personality and always put his team first. I wouldn't argue hard with anyone putting him in the top 5.

He's not top 5. Market has nothing to do with it since he was always pretty good to amazing. David Robinson to Manu to Parker to Leonard... TD didn't have the typical small market issues during his run with the team.
Shaq is better than Duncan wtf are you smoking

A little biased? Duncan is arguably the greatest PF, but he didn't do enough to be in the GOAT discussion. Kobe's in the same boat. He's 2nd greatest SG of all, and came up short. Both have 5. Both were considered the best, and one of the best players in the league at their peaks.

Well I think I personally would put the careers of MJ, Bron, Kareem, Russell, Wilt, Bird, Magic, Hakeem, then you get to splitting hairs between Duncan, Shaq, Kobe, I think I would put Curry up there. I can think of players that have more MVP's and finals MVP's and much better statistical impact.

Too many variables for a legit top 10 list. Kobe could, and should be in the top 10. That finals loss to the Celtics keeps him out of the top 10. I think he's top 10 but not top 5. It seems like the people that put him up there value his scoring and his flashiness over everything else

There is an entire generation of people that grew up with him around the world, with the development of the internet. And he played in one of the biggest sports organizations in the world. His face was everywhere and as a product he sold. When it comes to actual basketball impact I think it results in him being seen better than he was.
he did an excellent job of marketing himself, and because of that he brought more fans into the game. I just believe he is not as good of a player as people often consider him to be.
Seems to be a lot of people agree with my sentiment. Also Duncan did win 5 titles, more finals MVP's, more MVP's than Kobe and has a winning record over him, soooooo…..
He not only marketed himself but his greatest skill IMO is controlling his own narrative. I think his PR recovery after the Colorado incident was a greater achievement than those 5 rings.
He doesn't have to come by any of that without the five titles, to be fair. He rehabilitated his image and marketed his brand by WINNING. It all comes back to winning.

It was also sold to us that he was this guy that worked from nothing and that if you weren't a good player, it was because you didn't work as hard as him, and didn't want to win as much. People forgot he grew up wealthy, with a father who played NBA for near a decade.

Kobe is tricky. If anything, his intensity on the defensive end has been underrated at times. He wasn't shying away from the big defensive assignment in an era where that approach was gaining popularity. With that said, his game gloss over what a difficult teammate he could be. He would belittle teammates and demand loyalty for anyone who disagreed with him no matter how wrong he was. He gets a pass for some reason. Also, his championship teams were more stacked than people like to admit... Lamar Odom and Andrew Bynum are downright dominant at times.

Definitely Kobe. Especially after he died. People act like he carried a Laker team full of scrubs to a championship. They have Pau, Odom, and Artest on that team and they were in no way washed up back then. I doubt they'd win without Pau.
Thing is, they didn't win without Pau. Jumped from a barely .500 team to best in the best in one season. Pau led Kobe some years in some value metrics.

Yeah I think that is the key thing, I am not saying Kobe is bad or an average player. He achieved so much, consistently a top 3 player through large stretches of his career. But when it comes to being an all time great, it is a pretty competitive market.
Bull's Jordan is who Kobe thinks he is. Wizard's Jordan is who Kobe actually is.
